claims.text: The studied material is an additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy.
Atom probe tomography can elucidate nanoscale elemental redistribution associated with oxidation in this alloy.
High-temperature oxidation causes preferential elemental segregation at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Elemental segregation at nanoprecipitate interfaces influences the formation and integrity of the protective oxide scale.
Service-representative high-temperature oxidation can be modeled using elevated temperature and controlled oxygen partial pressure.
Nanoprecipitates and their interfaces act as the relevant structural mediator during oxidation.
Selective elemental diffusion during oxidation produces enrichment or depletion at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Interfacial enrichment or depletion alters oxide-scale formation and protective character.
APT measurements will reveal nanoscale elemental redistribution after oxidation.
Oxidation-resistant elements such as Cr or Al may become enriched at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
The observed elemental redistribution will correlate with enhanced oxidation performance of the additively manufactured alloy relative to cast or wrought counterparts.
APT can provide three-dimensional atomic-scale maps and quantitative measurements of elemental segregation at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
The hypothesis would be falsified if oxidized and unoxidized specimens show no significant difference in elemental distribution or no interface-specific segregation.
